chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'In seeking the world there is harm to the Hereafter, and in seeking the Hereafter there is harm to the world. So harm the world, for it is more deserving of harm.'
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between worldly life and the Hereafter according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in al-Kafi, articulates the Shia concept of 'zuhd' (asceticism) not as total renunciation, but as a strategic prioritization where the world is accepted as expendable to secure the Hereafter. Scholars interpret the 'harm' (idrar) to the world as a deliberate detachment from excessive attachment, ensuring that worldly pursuits do not become an idol that distracts from divine obligations. This reflects the balanced approach of the Ahl al-Bayt, who engaged with the world but kept their hearts anchored in the eternal.
